headline: Apple unveils the iPhone and drops 'Computer' from its name
text: On 9 January Steve Jobs presented the iPhone, a mobile phone, music player and internet device operated with the fingers on a touch screen, and Apple Computer renamed itself Apple Inc. The iPhone goes on sale in the United States in June.
imageCaption: Steve Jobs presents the iPhone, San Francisco, 9 January 2007

headline: CUDA: graphics chips for general computing
text: Nvidia released the first version of CUDA, software that lets programmers use its graphics processors for general calculations that can be split into many parallel parts, not just for drawing images.
imageCaption: The Nvidia GeForce 8800 GTX graphics card, introduced in November 2006

headline: Altria spins off Kraft
text: On 30 March Altria distributed its roughly 89% stake in Kraft Foods to its shareholders, about 0.7 Kraft share for each Altria share. Chairman Louis Camilleri says an independent Kraft can grow faster and make acquisitions with its own shares. Altria keeps the US and international cigarette businesses.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/764180/000119312507017014/dex991.htm (Altria press release of 31 January 2007, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altria (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Scandal takes down von Pierer and Kleinfeld
text: On 19 April supervisory board chairman Heinrich von Pierer said he will resign, denying any guilt over events during his time as chief executive. On 25 April chief executive Klaus Kleinfeld said he will not seek to renew his contract, which ends in September, after board members disagreed publicly about extending it.
imageCaption: Heinrich von Pierer, then Siemens' chief executive, 1994

headline: Amazon's profit more than doubles
text: On April 24 Amazon reported first-quarter sales of $3.02 billion, up 32%, and net income of $111 million, up 115%. Operating income rose 38%.
imageCaption: Jeff Bezos holds a copy of the first book Amazon sold, next to a sampling of the non-book goods it now sells, Seattle, 2005

headline: Nestlé buys Gerber baby food from Novartis
text: Nestlé agreed in April to buy the American baby food maker Gerber from Novartis for $5.5 billion. Gerber has most of the American baby food market. Nestlé is also buying Novartis's medical nutrition business for $2.5 billion.

headline: Chrysler is sold to Cerberus
text: On 14 May DaimlerChrysler agreed to sell 80.1% of Chrysler to the private-equity firm Cerberus in a deal valued at 7.4 billion dollars, keeping 19.9%. Chrysler lost 1.5 billion dollars in 2006 and announced 13,000 job cuts in February. DaimlerChrysler's shares rose on the news.
source: NBC News, 'Chrysler Group to be sold for $7.4 billion', 13-14 May 2007, https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna18645179 (read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2007 ('Spinoff of the Chrysler Group', 14 May 2007), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2007.xhtml?oid=4913464 (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Lehman joins a $22 billion apartment buyout
text: Lehman Brothers and the property firm Tishman Speyer agreed to buy Archstone-Smith, an owner of about 87,700 apartments in 359 communities, in a $22.2 billion deal.
imageCaption: Stuyvesant Town and Peter Cooper Village, New York

headline: The 787 Dreamliner is unveiled
text: Boeing showed its first 787 Dreamliner to about 15,000 people in Everett on 8 July, broadcast to 45 countries. It is the fastest-selling new jet in Boeing's history.
imageCaption: The first Boeing 787 Dreamliner, unveiled before a crowd at Everett, Washington, 8 July 2007

headline: 'As long as the music is playing, you've got to get up and dance'
text: Asked whether Citigroup would keep financing leveraged buyouts despite worries about credit markets, chief executive Charles Prince said: 'As long as the music is playing, you've got to get up and dance. We're still dancing.'
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Prince (read 2026-10-03, citing New York Times DealBook, 10 July 2007)
imageCaption: Chuck Prince, Citigroup's chief executive, at the World Economic Forum in Davos, January 2007, six months before his remark about dancing while the music plays
imageCredit: Ricardo Stuckert / Presidency of Brazil (Agência Brasil)

headline: Chief executive Peter Wuffli steps down
text: On 6 July Peter Wuffli unexpectedly stepped down as chief executive of UBS; Marcel Rohner succeeds him. In May UBS had closed Dillon Read Capital Management, its in-house hedge fund, after losses on US mortgage securities. Markets for such securities are now in turmoil.
imageCaption: Marcel Rohner, who succeeds Peter Wuffli as chief executive of UBS, July 2007

headline: Lehman shuts its subprime mortgage lender
text: Lehman Brothers is closing BNC Mortgage, its subprime home loan unit, cutting about 1,200 jobs in 23 locations, because market conditions 'necessitated a substantial reduction in its resources and capacity in the subprime space'. It will keep making mortgages through Aurora Loan Services. The shares fell 17% in July and another 12% in August.
imageCaption: Lehman Brothers headquarters, Times Square, New York, August 2007

headline: Credit markets freeze: BNP Paribas blocks funds, the Fed steps in
text: On 9 August the French bank BNP Paribas blocked withdrawals from three funds invested in American mortgage securities, citing 'a complete evaporation of liquidity'. Banks stopped trusting each other, and on 17 August the Federal Reserve cut its discount rate by half a point to 5.75 percent and offered banks loans of up to 30 days against mortgages and other collateral. Shares swung wildly but the S&P 500 ended August up 1%.
imageCaption: Traders on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange in the credit-crunch week, 16 August 2007
imageCredit: Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY/AFP via Getty Images

headline: The S&P 500 sets a record after Fed rate cuts
text: After the Federal Reserve cut its key rate by half a point to 4.75 percent in September, shares rallied, and the S&P 500 closed at a record 1,565.15 on 9 October, just above its 2000 peak. The Dow reached about 14,164. The Fed cut again on 31 October, to 4.5 percent.
imageCaption: A trader on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange goes for a high-five as the Dow reaches a record intraday high, 1 October 2007

headline: Citigroup warns of a 60% profit drop on mortgage losses
text: Citigroup warned on 1 October that dislocations in mortgage and credit markets would cut its third-quarter profit by about 60%, and on 15 October reported net income of $2.4 billion. On 31 October an analyst at CIBC, Meredith Whitney, said Citigroup was paying out more in dividends than it earned and might need to raise about $30 billion or cut its dividend.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000110465907072200/a07-24989_1ex99d1.htm (Citigroup press release, 1 October 2007; read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000110465907074791/a07-26588_1ex99d1.htm (15 October 2007; read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citigroup (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Citigroup Center on Lexington Avenue, New York

headline: DaimlerChrysler becomes Daimler
text: On 4 October an extraordinary shareholders' meeting approved renaming DaimlerChrysler AG as Daimler AG. The sale of Chrysler to Cerberus was completed on 3 August. The company now concentrates on Mercedes-Benz cars and on trucks, where it is the world's biggest maker.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2007 ('DaimlerChrysler AG becomes Daimler AG', 4 October 2007; 'Cerberus acquires majority of Chrysler Group', 3 August 2007), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2007.xhtml?oid=4913464 (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Nokia nearly doubles its profit
text: On 18 October Nokia reported third-quarter net profit of 1.56 billion euros, almost double a year earlier, with a 39% share of the world handset market, close to its long-stated goal of 40%. Sales were strong in India and China. Its shares jumped 7%.
imageCaption: The Nokia N95 8GB, Nokia's flagship smartphone

headline: Prince quits as Citigroup warns of up to $11 billion in write-downs
text: On 4 November Citigroup said the value of its $55 billion of subprime mortgage exposure, most of it in the top-rated slices of complex securities called CDOs, had fallen by $8-11 billion since September; Charles Prince resigned, with Robert Rubin as chairman and Sir Win Bischoff as acting chief executive. Citigroup said it had no plans to cut its dividend. On 26 November it sold $7.5 billion of securities convertible into shares to the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. The shares fell 21% in the month.
imageCaption: Chuck Prince, Citigroup's chief executive, at Davos, January 2007

headline: $10 billion more in write-downs; Singapore steps in
text: On 10 December UBS announced further write-downs of about $10 billion on US subprime mortgage positions and new capital of 13 billion francs: mandatory convertible notes sold to the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (11 billion) and an investor from the Middle East (2 billion). Shareholders get a stock dividend instead of a cash dividend for 2007. UBS expects a loss for the year.
source: UBS Form 20-F/A for 2007, filed 14 April 2008, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1114446/000095012308004121/y54449e20vfza.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/UBS (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Marcel Ospel, chairman of UBS, at the St. Gallen Symposium, 2003
